# Writing a script

Every mark a Generative or Synthesis script, or a Table brief, may carry - the list the script editor's palette (**Edit** on the panel) is built from, and the patterns it highlights with. A script is Markdown; YAML frontmatter at the top is the panel's and never shown in the editor or spoken. A Table brief is handed to the show's agents rather than read aloud, so a mark offered there says what it does in a brief.

ScriptMarks - every authoring mark a script may carry, registered with what it does.

A script is plain Markdown, and ghost reads more out of it than the words: speaker cues, hesitations, picture markers, inline pronunciations, template macros, emphasis. This is the one list: the `ScriptWriter` palette is built from it, `ScriptHighlighter` colors a script with its patterns, and docs.py writes docs/script.md from it.

An entry does not implement its mark. The parsers of record stay where they are (`Manuscript` for cues, rests and pictures; `TextNorm` and `Phonemes` for the rest), and `tests/notes/script_marks_check.gd` inserts every entry's example and asks those parsers what they make of it, so an entry that drifts from what the reader does fails there, and a new entry without a check fails too.

A table brief is not a script, and has marks of its own: a show's document is the brief its agents work from, never read aloud, so a mark in it does something only where the code reads it out of the brief or an agent is told to honor it. Those are offered ("table" in `modes`), each saying what it does there (`blurbs`): a speaker cue gives the show another voice, a `## Cards` section is its deck, a macro reads as its default and a note to self is taken out before any agent sees the brief (`TablePrompts.brief`), and a hesitation, a delivery or a stressed word stands in a line the brief gives the host word for word (rules/table/reader.yaml, `spoken`). The marks of a page or a tablet (pictures, scene lines, web pages) and the inline pronunciation are not offered: the table is the only medium there, and a reader's passage keeps no bracket (`TableProducer.clean_spoken`).

Registry: `ScriptMarks.REGISTRY` in [src/notes/script_marks.gd](../src/notes/script_marks.gd) (84 entries). Each one is proven against the parser that reads it by `tests/notes/script_marks_check.gd`.

## Voices

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speaker cue | `<!-- speaker: Name -->` | Generative, Table | Hands everything after it to the named voice, until the next cue. The panel's voices list follows the names the script uses. Must be a line of its own, or it is only a note. **In a Table brief:** Gives the show another voice by this name: a tab of its own on the Voice card, and the reader writes its lines and hands them over. Say in the brief who it is and when it speaks. Must be a line of its own. |
| Talk over | `<!-- over: 0.6 -->` | Generative, Table | At the top of a speaker's turn: this turn comes in before the last one has ended, on its last words, by a third of a second or the seconds given. Each voice stays where it sits, and both are heard. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives word for word, on the line after a speaker's cue: this turn comes in over the last. Elsewhere a game's master writes these with its tools. |
| All at once | `<!-- together -->` | Generative, Table | At the top of a speaker's turn: this turn comes in with the last one, just after it began, as a table reacts as one. Several in a row all come in together. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives word for word, on the line after a speaker's cue: this turn comes in with the last. Elsewhere a game's master writes these with its tools. |
| Heard through | `<!-- heard: radio -->` | Generative | On the line after a speaker's cue: this whole turn is heard through something - phone (held to the ear), desk (a phone lying on the desk), far (a voice in the caller's room, through their phone), radio (a two-way radio under crackling static, its squelch hissing as the voice keys up and off), receiver (a shortwave receiver: a voice from very far off inside the signal, sinking into its hiss and crackle as the signal fades) or tablet (a tablet's small speaker lying on the desk, brighter than a phone, no line's hiss). The band, the grit and the line's static are the voice's; a turn with none is heard in the room. A dispatch desk writes these itself; one written there wins. |

## Timing

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hesitation | `<!-- hesitation -->` | Generative, Table | A longer rest at exactly this point, mid-sentence included. Its length is the panel's Hesitate dial. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, a rest at exactly this point; its length is the Voice card's Hesitate dial. Everywhere else the reader places its own. |
| Delivery | `<!-- delivery: quicker, brighter -->` | Generative, Table | Lean how the rest of this paragraph is said, a step at a time: quicker / slower, brighter / graver, tighter / looser (pauses), louder / softer, or excited, serious, hushed, urgent, playful, tender, dry; steady is the voice's own. Small, and eased in and out over a few sentences. **In a Table brief:** On a line of its own before words the brief gives the host to say word for word: leans how they are said - quicker / slower, brighter / graver, tighter / looser, louder / softer, or excited, serious, hushed, urgent, playful, tender, dry. Everywhere else the reader chooses its own. |
| Timed hesitation | `<!-- hesitation: 2.5 -->` | Generative, Table | A rest of exactly this many seconds, whatever the Hesitate dial says. **In a Table brief:** In a line the brief gives the host to say word for word, a rest of exactly this many seconds. |
| Log-entry time | `21:40` | Generative | A time opening a paragraph is read as its heading, with a hesitation after it. The Notebook sets it in the margin. |
| Thinking hum | `Hmm.` | Generative | Hm, Hmm, Mmm as a sentence of their own are held to most of a second, settling and falling in pitch, instead of read as a clipped syllable. |
| Outro starts here | `<!-- outro -->` | Generative | The end begins at this point: the reading carries on but fades out - voice and picture together, over the Outro setting - and whatever text is left is cut. Own line or mid-sentence; the first one counts. |

## Pronunciation

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pronunciation | `[K AE T]` | Generative | Spells a word in ARPAbet phonemes, read exactly as written. For a name the voice gets wrong. |
| Say as | `<!-- say: Io-A = AY1 OW0 EY1 -->` | Generative, Song | How words are said, in ARPAbet (a vowel's stress its digit), wherever they come in the note - each still shown as written. For a name every voice gets wrong. IPA between slashes after it (`Gödel = G ER1 D AH0 L /ɡˈøːdl̩/`) is what a neural voice says instead, for a sound ARPAbet cannot spell. **In a Song brief:** How a word is sung, in ARPAbet (a vowel's stress its digit), wherever it comes in the song - still shown as written; its syllables and stress are the ones the tune is set to. IPA between slashes after it is what the voice sings instead, for a sound ARPAbet cannot spell. |
| Letter | `[a]` | Generative | A letter that names something - a number, a point, a case - said by its name and shown as the letter: [a] is "ay", where a bare a is read as the word a. |

| Template macro | `${CHAPTERS_BEFORE:twenty-one}` | Generative, Table | A placeholder for a fact only the book's build knows. Ghost Notes reads the default after the colon, never the macro itself; one with no default is skipped and named in the panel. **In a Table brief:** A placeholder for a fact only the build knows. The agents are handed the default after the colon, never the macro itself; one with no default is left out. |

A form after the name writes it so (YYYY, YY, MM, DD, MON for NOV); %nights since 2019-11-20% (or %days since ...) counts up to it, written 2,557. |

## The deck

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| The deck | `## Cards` | Table | Opens the show's own deck: every list item under this heading, down to the next heading of its level, is a card, and each episode's cards are a seeded shuffle of them. A brief with no such section leaves each episode's cards to the producer. |
| A suit | `### Major Arcana` | Table | Inside the deck: names the group the cards listed under it belong to - a suit, an arcana, a team. |
| A card | `- The Tower: sudden upheaval, a structure that was never sound` | Table | Inside the deck: one card - its name, then what it means after a colon. A numeral may lead it (XVI. The Tower). A writer is handed a card's meaning only once that card is drawn. |

| Note to self | `<!-- a note to yourself -->` | Generative, Table, Song | Any other HTML comment is an authoring note: never spoken, never printed. **In a Table brief:** Any other HTML comment is a note to yourself: taken out of the brief before any agent is handed it. **In a Song brief:** Any other HTML comment is a note to yourself: never sung, however many lines it runs over. |

## Song

| Mark | Example | Panels | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Song section | `<!-- chorus -->` | Song | Where a section of the song begins - verse, chorus or bridge (a pre-chorus plays as a bridge, a hook or refrain as a chorus) - on a line of its own; the lines under it are sung in it. Sections of a kind share their chords and their tune; a chorus lands hardest. With no lines under it, the last section of its kind is sung again (a chorus written once). |
| Instrumental section | `<!-- break: 8 -->` | Song | A section with no words, this many bars long, where it is written: intro, break (a solo, interlude or instrumental plays as a break - the lead takes the melody) or ending; bare, four bars. None of a kind written is drawn by the roll. Over a reference's form, its own bars between the sung sections stand instead. |
| Repeat | `<!-- repeat: 2 -->` | Song | The section so far sung again, on a line of its own: bare, twice in all; repeat: 3, three times in all. |
